outcome: Severe composite morbidity (reoperation, coagulopathy, thromboembolism, wound infection, multiorgan failure, transfusion reaction, fistula, or chest compressions)
cohort: 36 women with pathology-proven placentas accreta/increta/percreta from a single tertiary center from January 1, 2005 to December 31, 2012
finding: Although prenatally diagnosed cases of placenta accreta were more likely to be complex, both prenatally diagnosed and undiagnosed cases had statistically similar maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Prenatally diagnosed cases of placenta accreta were more likely to deliver by cesarean section compared to undiagnosed cases.
